name: CA-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Pete Aguilar running with $3.5M cash on hand
Challenger Stephanie Vargas has minimal reported fundraising
model.rationale: Aguilar holds a seat that leans Democratic by seven points, has raised $4.7M with no outside opposition spending, while his Republican challenger reports no fundraising. Markets price the incumbent near 95%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending against Aguilar would be the first sign the race is competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Pete Aguilar, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Southern California district that voted about seven points for Democrats at the presidential level. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised $4.7 million and holding $3.5 million on hand, with no outside groups spending against him. His Republican challenger, Stephanie Vargas, has no reported fundraising.

No public polls cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals: the district's lean, incumbency, and the money gap. Prediction markets price Aguilar's chances at roughly 95 percent. All signs point to a comfortable incumbent win, with the main uncertainty being the absence of direct polling rather than any evidence of a contest.
